title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: KS test compares empirical CDF generated angles theoretical CDF. Test statistic: \[D_N = \sup_{\theta \[0, \theta_0]} |\hat{F}_N(\theta) - F_\theta(\theta)|\] null hypothesis (correct distribution), \(\sqrt{N}D_N\) converges Kolmogorov distribution. finite precision, ties can occur sampled angles; apply tiny jitter KS test avoid spurious warnings, consistent verify_cone_uniformity().
code: #### Comprehensive KS test across dimensions and sample sizes            #### dimensions_ks <- c(2, 3, 5, 10, 20) sample_sizes_ks <- c(1000, 5000, 10000, 50000) theta0_ks <- pi/4  ks_results <- expand.grid(   dimension = dimensions_ks,   n_samples = sample_sizes_ks )  ks_results$ks_statistic <- NA ks_results$p_value <- NA  set.seed(42)  for (i in 1:nrow(ks_results)) {   n <- ks_results$dimension[i]   n_samp <- ks_results$n_samples[i]    mu_hat_ks <- c(rep(0, n-1), 1)   samples_ks <- generate_cone_samples(n_samp, mu_hat_ks, theta0_ks)   angles_ks <- acos(samples_ks[n, ])    #### Theoretical CDF                                                   ####   omega0_ks <- theta_to_omega(theta0_ks, n)   theoretical_cdf_ks <- function(theta) {     theta_to_omega(theta, n) / omega0_ks   }    angles_ks_test <- angles_ks   if (any(duplicated(angles_ks_test))) {     angles_ks_test <- jitter(angles_ks_test, amount = max(1e-12, .Machine$double.eps))     angles_ks_test <- pmax(0, pmin(theta0_ks, angles_ks_test))   }   ks_test_result <- ks.test(angles_ks_test, function(x) sapply(x, theoretical_cdf_ks), exact = FALSE)    ks_results$ks_statistic[i] <- as.numeric(ks_test_result$statistic)   ks_results$p_value[i] <- ks_test_result$p.value }  #### Summary statistics                                                  #### pass_rate <- sum(ks_results$p_value > 0.05) / nrow(ks_results) * 100  ks_results$result <- ifelse(ks_results$p_value > 0.05, "\u2714 Pass", "\u2718 Fail") knitr::kable(   ks_results,   digits = c(0, 0, 6, 4, NA),   col.names = c("dimension", "n samples", "KS statistic", "p-value", "result") ) summary_table <- data.frame(   metric = c("Overall pass rate", "Mean KS statistic", "Max KS statistic"),   value = c(     sprintf("%.1f%% (%d / %d)", pass_rate, sum(ks_results$p_value > 0.05), nrow(ks_results)),     sprintf("%.6f", mean(ks_results$ks_statistic)),     sprintf("%.6f", max(ks_results$ks_statistic))   ) ) knitr::kable(summary_table, col.names = c("metric", "value"))

title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Partition angle range bins test observed vs expected frequencies. Test statistic: \[\chi^2 = \sum_{=1}^k \frac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}\] \(O_i\) observed counts \(E_i\) expected counts bin . Chi-squared goodness--fit test: configuration. Uniformity diagnostics verify_cone_uniformity().
code: #### Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test                                    #### set.seed(42)  n_chi <- 5 theta0_chi <- pi/3 n_samples_chi <- 50000 n_bins <- 20  mu_hat_chi <- c(rep(0, n_chi-1), 1) samples_chi <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_chi, mu_hat_chi, theta0_chi) angles_chi <- acos(samples_chi[n_chi, ])  #### Verify using built-in function                                      #### verification <- verify_cone_uniformity(samples_chi, mu_hat_chi, theta0_chi, n_bins)  setup_chi_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Dimension n",                "Half-angle theta_0 (deg)"),   value = c(sprintf("%d", n_chi),             sprintf("%.0f", theta0_chi * 180/pi)) ) knitr::kable(setup_chi_table, caption = "Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test: configuration.") tests_table <- data.frame(   test = c("Kolmogorov-Smirnov",            "Chi-squared"),   statistic = c(sprintf("%.6f", verification$ks_statistic),                 sprintf("%.4f", verification$chi_squared)),   p_value = c(sprintf("%.4f", verification$ks_pvalue),               sprintf("%.4f", verification$chi_pvalue)),   result = c(ifelse(verification$ks_pvalue > 0.05, "uniform", "non-uniform"),              ifelse(verification$chi_pvalue > 0.05, "uniform", "non-uniform")) ) knitr::kable(tests_table, caption = "Uniformity diagnostics from verify_cone_uniformity().") library(ggplot2) theta_theory   <- seq(0, theta0_chi, length.out = 200) omega0_theory  <- theta_to_omega(theta0_chi, n_chi) s_n_minus_1    <- 2 * pi^((n_chi - 1) / 2) / gamma((n_chi - 1) / 2) s_n            <- 2 * pi^(n_chi / 2)        / gamma(n_chi / 2) df_theory      <- data.frame(   theta_deg = theta_theory * 180 / pi,   density   = (s_n_minus_1 / (s_n * omega0_theory)) *               sin(theta_theory)^(n_chi - 2) * (pi / 180) )  ggplot(data.frame(theta_deg = verification$angles * 180 / pi),        aes(theta_deg)) +   geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = n_bins,                  fill = "#3B528B", colour = "white") +   geom_line(data = df_theory, aes(theta_deg, density),             colour = "#E15759", linewidth = 0.9) +   labs(title    = sprintf("Observed vs. theoretical distribution (n = %d)", n_chi),        subtitle = "Empirical density vs. f_theta(theta)",        x = expression(paste(theta, " (degrees)")),        y = "density",        caption = "Source: verify_cone_uniformity() vs. analytic PDF.") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))

title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Test algorithm extremely high dimensions rejection sampling infeasible.  Linear scaling test: time = intercept + slope * n.
code: #### Validate in high dimensions                                         #### dimensions_high <- c(10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500) theta0_high <- pi/6 n_samples_high <- 10000  validation_results <- data.frame(   dimension = integer(),   mean_angle = numeric(),   sd_angle = numeric(),   ks_statistic = numeric(),   ks_pvalue = numeric(),   time_seconds = numeric() )  set.seed(42)  for (n_high in dimensions_high) {   mu_hat_high <- c(rep(0, n_high-1), 1)    time_start <- Sys.time()   samples_high <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_high, mu_hat_high, theta0_high,                                         method = "rejection")   time_elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), time_start, units = "secs"))    angles_high <- acos(samples_high[n_high, ])    #### Theoretical CDF                                                   ####   omega0_high <- theta_to_omega(theta0_high, n_high)   theoretical_cdf_high <- function(theta) {     theta_to_omega(theta, n_high) / omega0_high   }    ks_high <- ks.test(angles_high, function(x) sapply(x, theoretical_cdf_high))    validation_results <- rbind(validation_results, data.frame(     dimension = n_high,     mean_angle = mean(angles_high),     sd_angle = sd(angles_high),     ks_statistic = as.numeric(ks_high$statistic),     ks_pvalue = ks_high$p.value,     time_seconds = time_elapsed   ))  }  knitr::kable(   validation_results,   digits = c(0, 6, 6, 6, 4, 3),   col.names = c("dimension", "mean angle", "sd angle",                 "KS statistic", "p-value", "time (s)") ) summary_high_dim <- data.frame(   metric = "Tests with p > 0.05",   value = sprintf("%d / %d", sum(validation_results$ks_pvalue > 0.05),                   nrow(validation_results)) ) knitr::kable(summary_high_dim, col.names = c("metric", "value")) library(ggplot2); library(patchwork) theme_v <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))  p1 <- ggplot(validation_results, aes(dimension, mean_angle * 180 / pi)) +   geom_line(colour = "#3B528B", linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_point(colour = "#3B528B", size = 2.4) +   geom_hline(yintercept = mean(validation_results$mean_angle) * 180 / pi,              colour = "#E15759", linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.5) +   labs(title = "Mean angle consistency", x = "dimension",        y = "mean angle (degrees)") + theme_v  p2 <- ggplot(validation_results, aes(dimension, sd_angle * 180 / pi)) +   geom_line(colour = "#21908C", linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_point(colour = "#21908C", size = 2.4) +   labs(title = "Angle dispersion", x = "dimension",        y = "SD angle (degrees)") + theme_v  p3 <- ggplot(validation_results, aes(dimension, ks_pvalue)) +   geom_line(colour = "#9B5DE5", linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_point(colour = "#9B5DE5", size = 2.4) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, colour = "#E15759",              linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.5) +   labs(title = "Uniformity test p-values",        subtitle = expression(alpha == 0.05),        x = "dimension", y = "KS p-value") + theme_v  p4 <- ggplot(validation_results, aes(dimension, time_seconds)) +   geom_line(colour = "#F89540", linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_point(colour = "#F89540", size = 2.4) +   labs(title = sprintf("Computation time (N = %d)", n_samples_high),        x = "dimension", y = "time (seconds)",        caption = "Source: generate_cone_samples() under verify_cone_uniformity().") +   theme_v  (p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) #### Linear scaling verification                                         #### fit_time <- lm(time_seconds ~ dimension, data = validation_results) scaling_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Intercept",                "Slope (per dimension)",                "R-squared"),   value = c(sprintf("%.4f", coef(fit_time)[1]),             sprintf("%.6f", coef(fit_time)[2]),             sprintf("%.4f", summary(fit_time)$r.squared)) ) knitr::kable(scaling_table, caption = "Linear scaling test: time = intercept + slope * n.")

title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: cases analytical formulas exist, compare generated samples known solid angles. Test 1: 3D orthant (analytical Omega = 1/8, N = 100,000). Test 2: circular cone (Van Oosterom, N = 100,000). Test 3: hollow cone (annular region, n = 5, N = 50,000).
code: #### Compare with known analytical formulas                              #### #### Test case 1: Orthant in 3D                                          #### n_test1 <- 3 theta0_test1 <- pi/2 n_samples_test1 <- 100000  mu_hat_test1 <- c(1, 1, 1) / sqrt(3) samples_test1 <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_test1, mu_hat_test1, theta0_test1)  #### Count fraction within orthant                                       #### in_orthant <- apply(samples_test1, 2, function(x) all(x > 0)) omega_estimated <- sum(in_orthant) / n_samples_test1  omega_analytical <- 1/8  test1_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Analytical Omega",                "Estimated Omega",                "Absolute error",                "Relative error (%)",                "Standard error"),   value = c(sprintf("%.6f", omega_analytical),             sprintf("%.6f", omega_estimated),             sprintf("%.2e", abs(omega_estimated - omega_analytical)),             sprintf("%.2f", abs(omega_estimated - omega_analytical) /                               omega_analytical * 100),             sprintf("%.2e", sqrt(omega_estimated * (1 - omega_estimated) /                                  n_samples_test1))) ) knitr::kable(test1_table, caption = "Test 1: 3D orthant (analytical Omega = 1/8, N = 100,000).") #### Test case 2: Circular cone                                          #### theta0_test2 <- pi/4  # 45-degree cone omega_analytical_2 <- solid_angle_cone(theta0_test2)  n_test2 <- 3 n_samples_test2 <- 100000 mu_hat_test2 <- c(0, 0, 1)  samples_test2 <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_test2, mu_hat_test2, theta0_test2) angles_test2 <- acos(samples_test2[3, ])  #### All samples should be within cone                                   #### within_cone <- sum(angles_test2 <= theta0_test2) omega_estimated_2 <- theta_to_omega(theta0_test2, n_test2)  test2_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Analytical (Van Oosterom) Omega",                "Estimated (theta->omega) Omega",                "Absolute error",                "Relative error (%)",                "Samples within cone"),   value = c(sprintf("%.6f", omega_analytical_2),             sprintf("%.6f", omega_estimated_2),             sprintf("%.2e", abs(omega_estimated_2 - omega_analytical_2)),             sprintf("%.2f", abs(omega_estimated_2 - omega_analytical_2) /                               omega_analytical_2 * 100),             sprintf("%d / %d (%.2f%%)", within_cone, n_samples_test2,                     within_cone / n_samples_test2 * 100)) ) knitr::kable(test2_table, caption = "Test 2: circular cone (Van Oosterom, N = 100,000).") #### Test case 3: Hollow cone                                            #### theta1_test3 <- pi/6  # 30 degrees (inner) theta2_test3 <- pi/3  # 60 degrees (outer) n_test3 <- 5 n_samples_test3 <- 50000  mu_hat_test3 <- c(rep(0, n_test3-1), 1) samples_test3 <- replicate(n_samples_test3,                             generate_hollow_cone_sample(mu_hat_test3, theta1_test3, theta2_test3))  angles_test3 <- acos(samples_test3[n_test3, ])  omega1 <- theta_to_omega(theta1_test3, n_test3) omega2 <- theta_to_omega(theta2_test3, n_test3) omega_analytical_3 <- omega2 - omega1  #### Check all samples in range                                          #### in_range <- sum(angles_test3 >= theta1_test3 & angles_test3 <= theta2_test3)  test3_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Inner angle theta_1 (deg)",                "Omega_1",                "Outer angle theta_2 (deg)",                "Omega_2",                "Hollow cone Omega = Omega_2 - Omega_1",                "Samples in range",                "Mean angle (deg)",                "Expected mean angle (deg)"),   value = c(sprintf("%.0f", theta1_test3 * 180/pi),             sprintf("%.6f", omega1),             sprintf("%.0f", theta2_test3 * 180/pi),             sprintf("%.6f", omega2),             sprintf("%.6f", omega_analytical_3),             sprintf("%d / %d (%.2f%%)", in_range, n_samples_test3,                     in_range / n_samples_test3 * 100),             sprintf("%.0f", mean(angles_test3) * 180/pi),             sprintf("%.0f", (theta1_test3 + theta2_test3)/2 * 180/pi)) ) knitr::kable(test3_table, caption = "Test 3: hollow cone (annular region, n = 5, N = 50,000).")

what: Application 1: Monte Carlo integration on spherical domains
title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Compute integral function spherical cap. Monte Carlo integration spherical cap.
code: #### Monte Carlo integration on spherical cap                            #### #### Define test function: f(x) = exp(-||x - mu||^2)                     #### mu_center <- c(0, 0, 1) f_integrand <- function(x) {   exp(-sum((x - mu_center)^2)) }  n_app1 <- 3 theta0_app1 <- pi/3  # 60-degree cone n_samples_app1 <- 100000  mu_hat_app1 <- c(0, 0, 1) samples_app1 <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_app1, mu_hat_app1, theta0_app1)  #### Evaluate function at samples                                        #### function_values <- apply(samples_app1, 2, f_integrand)  #### Estimate integral                                                   #### omega_cap <- theta_to_omega(theta0_app1, n_app1) * 4 * pi  # In steradians integral_estimate <- omega_cap * mean(function_values) integral_se <- omega_cap * sd(function_values) / sqrt(n_samples_app1)  mc_app_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Integrand",                "Domain theta_0 (deg)",                "Samples N",                "Integral estimate",                "95% CI lower",                "95% CI upper",                "Relative SE (%)"),   value = c("exp(-||x_hat - mu||^2)",             sprintf("%.0f", theta0_app1 * 180/pi),             sprintf("%d", n_samples_app1),             sprintf("%.6f +/- %.6f", integral_estimate, 1.96 * integral_se),             sprintf("%.6f", integral_estimate - 1.96 * integral_se),             sprintf("%.6f", integral_estimate + 1.96 * integral_se),             sprintf("%.2f", integral_se / integral_estimate * 100)) ) knitr::kable(mc_app_table, caption = "Monte Carlo integration over a spherical cap.") library(ggplot2); library(patchwork) df_xy <- data.frame(X = samples_app1[1, ],                     Y = samples_app1[2, ],                     f = function_values)  theme_v <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))  p_xy <- ggplot(df_xy, aes(X, Y, colour = f)) +   geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +   scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "f(x)", option = "C") +   coord_fixed() +   labs(title    = "Function values over spherical cap",        subtitle = "XY projection of samples coloured by integrand",        x = "X", y = "Y") + theme_v  p_hist <- ggplot(data.frame(f = function_values), aes(f)) +   geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50,                  fill = "#3B528B", colour = "white") +   geom_vline(xintercept = mean(function_values), colour = "#E15759",              linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.7) +   labs(title    = "Distribution of function values",        subtitle = "Empirical density; dashed red = sample mean",        x = expression(paste("f(", hat(x), ")")),        y = "density",        caption = "Source: Monte Carlo integration over a spherical cap.") + theme_v  p_xy + p_hist

what: Application 2: Directional statistics and von Mises-Fisher distribution
title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Generate samples directional distributions spheres. von Mises-Fisher parameters cone threshold. Importance-sampling diagnostics vMF approximation.
code: #### Simulate von Mises-Fisher distribution using cone sampling          #### #### Von Mises-Fisher PDF: f(x) \u221D exp(\u03BA x^T \u03BC)                         #### n_vmf <- 3 mu_vmf <- c(0, 0, 1) kappa_vmf <- 5  # Concentration parameter  #### Approximate 99% of mass within cone                                 #### #### For VMF: E[angle] \u2248 arccos(1/\u03BA) for large \u03BA                    #### theta_approx <- acos(0.01^(1/kappa_vmf))  # Approximate threshold n_samples_vmf <- 10000  vmf_params_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Dimension n",                "Mean direction mu",                "Concentration kappa",                "Cone half-angle theta_0 (deg)"),   value = c(sprintf("%d", n_vmf),             paste(sprintf("%.1f", mu_vmf), collapse = ", "),             sprintf("%.1f", kappa_vmf),             sprintf("%.0f", theta_approx * 180/pi)) ) knitr::kable(vmf_params_table, caption = "von Mises-Fisher parameters and cone threshold.") #### Generate samples                                                    #### samples_vmf <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_vmf, mu_vmf, theta_approx)  #### Compute importance weights                                          #### dot_products <- samples_vmf[3, ] uniform_pdf <- 1 / (4 * pi) vmf_pdf_unnorm <- exp(kappa_vmf * dot_products)  #### Normalize                                                           #### c_kappa <- kappa_vmf / (4 * pi * sinh(kappa_vmf))  # Normalization constant vmf_pdf <- c_kappa * vmf_pdf_unnorm  weights <- vmf_pdf / uniform_pdf weights_normalized <- weights / sum(weights)  #### Effective sample size                                               #### ess <- 1 / sum(weights_normalized^2)  vmf_stats_table <- data.frame(   quantity = c("Mean weight",                "SD weights",                "Effective sample size",                "ESS fraction (%)"),   value = c(sprintf("%.6f", mean(weights)),             sprintf("%.6f", sd(weights)),             sprintf("%.0f", ess),             sprintf("%.1f", ess / n_samples_vmf * 100)) ) knitr::kable(vmf_stats_table, caption = "Importance-sampling diagnostics for vMF approximation.") library(ggplot2); library(patchwork) angles_vmf       <- acos(dot_products) weighted_breaks  <- seq(0, max(angles_vmf * 180 / pi), length.out = 31) weighted_bins    <- cut(angles_vmf * 180 / pi, breaks = weighted_breaks,                          include.lowest = TRUE) weighted_density <- tapply(weights, weighted_bins, sum) weighted_density[is.na(weighted_density)] <- 0 weighted_density <- weighted_density / sum(weighted_density) /                     diff(weighted_breaks)[1] df_weighted <- data.frame(   mid     = weighted_breaks[-length(weighted_breaks)] +             diff(weighted_breaks) / 2,   density = as.numeric(weighted_density) )  theme_v <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))  p_w <- ggplot(data.frame(weights), aes(weights)) +   geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50,                  fill = "#3B528B", colour = "white") +   labs(title = "Distribution of importance weights",        x = "weight", y = "density") + theme_v  p_a <- ggplot(data.frame(theta_deg = angles_vmf * 180 / pi),               aes(theta_deg)) +   geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50,                  fill = "#21908C", colour = "white") +   labs(title = "Angle from mean direction",        x = expression(paste(theta, " (degrees)")),        y = "density") + theme_v  p_xy <- ggplot(data.frame(X = samples_vmf[1, ], Y = samples_vmf[2, ],                            w = weights),                aes(X, Y, colour = w)) +   geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +   scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "vMF density", option = "C") +   coord_fixed() +   labs(title = "Samples coloured by vMF density", x = "X", y = "Y") + theme_v  p_wh <- ggplot(df_weighted, aes(mid, density)) +   geom_col(fill = "#F89540", colour = "white") +   labs(title = "Weighted angle distribution",        x = expression(paste(theta, " (degrees)")),        y = "weighted density",        caption = "Source: importance sampling on the spherical cap.") + theme_v  (p_w + p_a) / (p_xy + p_wh)

what: Application 3: Ray tracing and computer graphics
title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Efficient sampling reflected rays within hemisphere. Lambertian reflection scene.
code: #### Ray tracing: Lambertian reflectance                                 #### surface_normal <- c(0, 0, 1) incident_ray   <- c(0.3, 0.2, -1) incident_ray   <- incident_ray / sqrt(sum(incident_ray^2))  #### Generate reflected rays on the upper hemisphere                     #### #### For Lambertian: PDF proportional to cos(theta) = n_hat . r_hat       #### n_rays         <- 5000 reflected_rays <- generate_cone_samples(n_rays, surface_normal, pi / 2) cos_theta_rays <- reflected_rays[3, ] all_in_hem     <- all(cos_theta_rays >= 0)  scene_summary <- data.frame(   quantity = c("surface normal n_hat",                "incident ray i_hat",                "number of reflected rays",                "mean cos(theta) (expected 0.5)",                "all rays in upper hemisphere"),   value    = c(paste(sprintf("%.1f", surface_normal), collapse = ", "),                paste(sprintf("%.2f", incident_ray),   collapse = ", "),                sprintf("%d", n_rays),                sprintf("%.4f", mean(cos_theta_rays)),                ifelse(all_in_hem, "yes", "no")) ) knitr::kable(scene_summary, caption = "Lambertian reflection scene.") #### Side-view projection (XZ plane)                                     #### rays_df    <- data.frame(x = reflected_rays[1, ], z = reflected_rays[3, ]) surface_df <- data.frame(x = c(-1, 1), z = c(0, 0)) arrow_df <- data.frame(   role  = factor(c("incident", "normal"),                  levels = c("incident", "normal")),   x0    = c(0,                         0),   z0    = c(0.5,                       0),   x1    = c(incident_ray[1] / 2,       0),   z1    = c(0.5 + incident_ray[3] / 2, 0.5) ) label_df <- data.frame(   role  = arrow_df$role,   x     = c(arrow_df$x1[1] - 0.05, arrow_df$x1[2] + 0.04),   z     = c(arrow_df$z1[1],        arrow_df$z1[2]),   label = c("incident",            "normal") )  p_side <- ggplot() +   geom_point(data = rays_df, aes(x, z),              colour = "#3B528B", alpha = 0.25, size = 0.6) +   geom_path(data = surface_df, aes(x, z),             colour = "black", linewidth = 1.0) +   geom_segment(data = arrow_df,                aes(x = x0, y = z0, xend = x1, yend = z1, colour = role),                arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 0.9) +   geom_text(data = label_df, aes(x, z, label = label, colour = role),             show.legend = FALSE, size = 3.4) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(incident = "#E64B35", normal = "#1B7837"),                       name = NULL) +   coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +   labs(x = "X", y = "Z (up)",        title    = "Reflected rays (side view)",        subtitle = "XZ projection of 5000 hemisphere samples",        caption  = "Source: generate_cone_samples(n_rays, n_hat, pi/2).") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.caption    = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0),         legend.position = "top")  #### Angular distribution against the uniform-hemisphere PDF             #### angles_deg <- acos(cos_theta_rays) * 180 / pi theta_th   <- seq(0, pi / 2, length.out = 200) pdf_rad    <- sin(theta_th) pdf_rad    <- pdf_rad / (sum(pdf_rad) * (theta_th[2] - theta_th[1])) pdf_deg    <- pdf_rad * (pi / 180) theory_df  <- data.frame(theta_deg = theta_th * 180 / pi,                          density   = pdf_deg)  p_dist <- ggplot() +   geom_histogram(data = data.frame(theta_deg = angles_deg),                  aes(theta_deg, after_stat(density)),                  bins = 30, fill = "#21908C", colour = "white",                  alpha = 0.85) +   geom_line(data = theory_df, aes(theta_deg, density),             colour = "#E64B35", linewidth = 1.0) +   labs(x = expression(paste(theta, " from normal (degrees)")),        y = "density",        title    = "Distribution of reflection angles",        subtitle = "histogram of simulated angles vs the uniform-hemisphere PDF sin(theta)",        caption  = "Source: generate_cone_samples(); red curve is the theoretical sin(theta) density.") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))  p_side + p_dist note_df <- data.frame(   note = paste("For true cosine-weighted hemisphere sampling (Lambertian),",                "an additional importance sampling step would weight each ray",                "by cos(theta).") ) knitr::kable(note_df, col.names = "note")

title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Scaling analysis generate_cone_samples().
code: #### Analyze computational cost vs accuracy trade-off                    #### n_perf <- 10 theta0_perf <- pi/4 sample_sizes_perf <- 10^seq(2, 6, by = 0.3)  mu_hat_perf <- c(rep(0, n_perf-1), 1)  #### True solid angle (for error computation)                            #### omega_true_perf <- theta_to_omega(theta0_perf, n_perf)  results_perf <- data.frame(   n_samples = integer(),   time_seconds = numeric(),   mean_angle = numeric(),   sd_angle = numeric() )  set.seed(42)  for (n_samp in round(sample_sizes_perf)) {   t_start <- Sys.time()   samples_perf <- generate_cone_samples(n_samp, mu_hat_perf, theta0_perf)   t_elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t_start, units = "secs"))    #### Compute angle statistics                                          ####   angles_perf <- acos(samples_perf[n_perf, ])   mean_angle <- mean(angles_perf)   sd_angle <- sd(angles_perf)    results_perf <- rbind(results_perf, data.frame(     n_samples = n_samp,     time_seconds = t_elapsed,     mean_angle = mean_angle,     sd_angle = sd_angle   )) }  knitr::kable(   results_perf,   digits = c(0, 4, 6, 6),   col.names = c("n samples", "time (s)", "mean angle (rad)", "sd angle") ) library(ggplot2); library(patchwork) fit_scaling   <- lm(log10(time_seconds) ~ log10(n_samples), data = results_perf) slope_scaling <- coef(fit_scaling)[2] results_perf$pred_time <- 10^predict(fit_scaling) results_perf$time_per_sample_us <- results_perf$time_seconds /                                     results_perf$n_samples * 1e6 results_perf$ref_sd <- results_perf$sd_angle[1] *                        sqrt(results_perf$n_samples[1] / results_perf$n_samples)  theme_v <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))  p_time <- ggplot(results_perf, aes(n_samples, time_seconds)) +   geom_line(colour = "#3B528B", linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_point(colour = "#3B528B", size = 2.4) + title: Uniform Monte Carlo sampling on n-dimensional spheres and spherical caps
text: Direct comparison O(n) algorithm vs naive rejection.
code: #### Compare O(n) vs rejection sampling                                  #### dimensions_comp <- c(2, 3, 6) theta0_comp_rej <- pi/12  # 15-degree cone (narrow) n_samples_target <- 10000  comparison_results <- data.frame(   dimension = integer(),   time_on = numeric(),   time_rejection = numeric(),   speedup = numeric(),   expected_rejections = numeric() )  set.seed(42)  for (n_comp_rej in dimensions_comp) {   mu_hat_comp_rej <- c(rep(0, n_comp_rej-1), 1)    #### O(n) algorithm                                                    ####   t_on <- system.time({     samples_on <- generate_cone_samples(n_samples_target, mu_hat_comp_rej,                                         theta0_comp_rej, method = "inverse")   })[3]    #### Rejection sampling                                                ####   omega_comp <- theta_to_omega(theta0_comp_rej, n_comp_rej)   expected_total <- n_samples_target / omega_comp    t_rejection <- system.time({     samples_rej <- matrix(0, nrow = n_comp_rej, ncol = n_samples_target)     count <- 0     attempts <- 0      while (count < n_samples_target && attempts < expected_total * 10) {       #### Generate on full sphere                                       ####       z <- rnorm(n_comp_rej)       candidate <- z / sqrt(sum(z^2))        #### Test if within cone                                           ####       if (candidate[n_comp_rej] >= cos(theta0_comp_rej)) {         count <- count + 1         samples_rej[, count] <- candidate       }       attempts <- attempts + 1     }   })[3]    speedup <- t_rejection / t_on    comparison_results <- rbind(comparison_results, data.frame(     dimension = n_comp_rej,     time_on = t_on,     time_rejection = t_rejection,     speedup = speedup,     expected_rejections = expected_total   )) }  knitr::kable(   comparison_results,   digits = c(0, 4, 4, 1, 0),   col.names = c("dimension", "O(n) time", "rejection time",                 "speedup", "expected samples") ) library(ggplot2); library(patchwork) theme_v <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8, hjust = 0))  p_speed <- ggplot(comparison_results, aes(dimension, speedup)) +   geom_line(colour = "#E15759", linewidth = 0.9) +   geom_point(colour = "#E15759", size = 2.4) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey60",              linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.4) +   scale_y_log10() +   labs(title    = bquote("O(n) vs rejection (" * theta[0] * " = " *                             .(sprintf("%.0f", theta0_comp_rej * 180 / pi)) * degree * ")"),        subtitle = "Speedup factor of structured vs naive rejection sampler",        x = "dimension", y = "speedup factor") + theme_v  p_cost <- ggplot(comparison_results,                   aes(dimension, log10(expected_rejections))) +   geom_line(colour = "#3B528B", linewidth = 0.9) +   geom_point(colour = "#3B528B", size = 2.4) +   labs(title    = "Rejection sampling cost",        subtitle = "Log10 of expected full-sphere samples per accepted in-cap sample",        x = "dimension",        y = expression(log[10] * "(expected samples)"),        caption = "Source: empirical timing of generate_cone_samples() vs. naive rejection.") + theme_v  p_speed + p_cost

title: SolidAngleR - Computing normalized solid angles of polyhedral cones in arbitrary dimensions
text: normalized solid angle measure \(\tilde{\Omega}_n(C)\) polyhedral cone \(C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\) quantifies proportion \(n\)-dimensional space occupied cone. Formally: \[\tilde{\Omega}_n(C) = \frac{\text{vol}_{n-1}(C \cap S^{n-1})}{\text{vol}_{n-1}(S^{n-1})}\] \(S^{n-1}\) unit sphere \(\mathbb{R}^n\). 2D (\(n=2\)), \(\tilde{\Omega}_2 = \frac{\theta}{2\pi}\), \(\theta\) planar angle radians. 3D (\(n=3\)), \(\tilde{\Omega}_3 = \frac{\Omega}{4\pi}\), \(\Omega\) standard solid angle steradians. n-D, \(\tilde{\Omega}_n\) represents fraction unit hypersphere surface covered cone.

title: SolidAngleR - Computing normalized solid angles of polyhedral cones in arbitrary dimensions
text: normalized solid angle several fundamental properties. range \(\tilde{\Omega}_n(C) \[0, 1]\); orthant (axes-aligned cone), \(\tilde{\Omega}_n(\mathbb{R}^n_{\geq 0}) = \frac{1}{2^n}\); full space, \(\tilde{\Omega}_n(\mathbb{R}^n) = 1\); empty cone, \(\tilde{\Omega}_n(\emptyset) = 0\).

title: Compute the normalized solid angle of a polyhedral cone — compute_solid_angle
text: V numeric matrix whose columns cone generators. simplicial cone matrix square (\(n \times n\)) linearly independent columns. method Character scalar selecting backend. Allowed values: "auto": automatic selection based dimension spectrum associated matrix (default). "formula": closed-form analytical formula. Available \(n = 2\) (planar arc length) \(n = 3\) (Van Oosterom- Strackee tetrahedron formula). "series": Ribando's hypergeometric series. Requires associated matrix \(M_n(C)\) positive definite. "tridiagonal": Fitisone-Zhou tridiagonal series. Requires Gram matrix \(V^\top V\) tridiagonal. "decomposition": Fitisone-Zhou signed decomposition sub-cones positive definite associated matrices. "mvn": integration zero-mean multivariate normal covariance \(B^{-1}\) positive orthant via mvtnorm::pmvnorm() (Genz-Bretz quasi-Monte Carlo). max_terms Integer. Maximum number terms used series decomposition backends truncation. Default 1000. tol Numeric. Convergence tolerance iterative backends. Default 1e-10. normalize Logical. TRUE (default) input vectors rescaled unit Euclidean norm geometric computation.

title: Compute the normalized solid angle of a polyhedral cone — compute_solid_angle
text: single numeric value \([0, 1]\) giving fraction unit sphere \(S^{n-1}\) covered cone. orthant dimension \(n\) returns \(1/2^n\).

title: Compute the normalized solid angle of a polyhedral cone — compute_solid_angle
text: dispatcher implements method selection Fitisone & Zhou (2023) series decomposition routes, closed-form formulas Van Oosterom & Strackee (1983) low dimensions, Genz-Bretz quasi-Monte Carlo orthant integration Genz & Bretz (2009) multivariate-normal route. \(n = 2\) cone reduces planar wedge opening angle \(\theta\) normalized solid angle \(\Omega = \theta / (2\pi)\). \(n = 3\) dispatcher uses Van Oosterom-Strackee formula $$E = 2 \arctan\left(\frac{|v_1 \cdot (v_2 \times v_3)|}{1 + v_1 \cdot v_2 + v_2 \cdot v_3 + v_3 \cdot v_1}\right),$$ giving \(\Omega = E / (4\pi)\). \(n \geq 4\) positive definite associated matrix dispatcher selects Ribando's hypergeometric series (Theorem 1.5 Ribando 2006); Gram matrix additionally tridiagonal, simplified series Fitisone & Zhou (2023, Theorem 4.1) preferred lower per-term cost. associated matrix positive definite, cone decomposed Theorem 3.3 Corollary 3.4 Fitisone & Zhou (2023) signed sub-cones whose individual solid angles computed series route aggregated. "mvn" branch computes \(B = V^\top V\), recovers covariance \(\Sigma = B^{-1}\), integrates centred Gaussian covariance positive orthant: $$\Omega = \int_{[0, \infty)^n} \phi_n(x;\, 0,\, \Sigma)\, dx,$$ \(\phi_n\) \(n\)-variate normal density. integral evaluated Genz-Bretz lattice rule random shifts implemented mvtnorm::pmvnorm(), achieving effective convergence rate close \(O(N^{-1})\) sufficiently smooth integrands. Numerical safeguards: condition number \(\kappa(B) > 10^{10}\) "mvn" branch issues warning. ambient dimension \(n > 20\) high-dimension warning also emitted, since series cost orthant integration accuracy degrade rapidly. Symmetries measure: normalized solid angle invariant () orthogonal transformation ambient space, \(\Omega(QV) = \Omega(V)\) \(Q \O(n)\), includes antipodal symmetry \(\Omega(-V) = \Omega(V)\) special case \(Q = -\); (ii) positive scaling column, \(\Omega(V\,\mathrm{diag}(d_1, \ldots, d_n)) = \Omega(V)\) \(d_i > 0\), since cone determined rays, column lengths; (iii) permutation columns, relabels generators. invariances exact hold every backend; "mvn" route follow fact \(V \mapsto -V\) column scaling leave \(V^\top V\) invariant (normalization), integrand integration region Genz-Bretz orthant probability unchanged.

text: Theorem 3.3 Fitisone & Zhou (2023), simplicial cone admits decomposition \((n-1)!\) sub-cones (Corollary 3.4), falling one two terminal classes: () affine dimension strictly less \(n\), contributing zero solid angle; (II) positive definite associated matrix, Ribando's series (Theorem 1.5) converges sub-cone admits exact computation. reconstruction identity $$\Omega_n(C) = \sum_{} s_i \cdot \Omega_n(C_i),$$ \(s_i \\{-1, +1\}\) signs returned signs \(C_i\) cones returned cones. wrapper solid_angle_decomposition performs aggregation. title: Solid angle via Ribando's multivariable hypergeometric series — hypergeometric_series
text: Ribando-Aomoto series (equation 5 Ribando 2006, equation 1 Fitisone & Zhou 2023) $$\Omega(C) = \frac{|\det V|}{(4\pi)^{n/2}} \sum_{\\mathbb{N}_0^N}         \frac{(-2)^{||}}{!}\, \prod_{=1}^n \Gamma\!\left(\frac{1 + \deg_i()}{2}\right)\,         \alpha^{},$$ \(N = \binom{n}{2}\), \(= (a_{ij})_{<j}\) multi-index pairs generator indices, \(|| = \sum_{<j} a_{ij}\), \(\deg_i() = \sum_{k \neq } a_{ik}\), \(\alpha_{ij} = v_i \cdot v_j\). series converges absolutely \(\Omega(C)\) associated matrix \(M_n(C) = (m_{ij})\) \(m_{ii} = 1\) \(m_{ij} = -|\alpha_{ij}|\) \(\neq j\) positive definite (Ribando 2006, Theorem 1.5). implementation enumerates terms total degree \(||\) truncation error cut-can bounded contribution next degree level. \(n = 2, 3\) dispatcher delegates specialised implementations exploit small number pair indices.

title: General n-dimensional Ribando series for solid angle — hypergeometric_series_nd
text: Mathematical Formulation: function computes series: $$T_{\alpha} = \frac{|\det V|}{(4\pi)^{n/2}} \sum_{\mathbf{} \\mathbb{N}_0^N} \left[ \frac{(-2)^{|\mathbf{}|}}{\mathbf{}!} \prod_{=1}^n \Gamma\left(\frac{1 + \text{deg}_i(\mathbf{})}{2}\right) \right] \alpha^{\mathbf{}}$$ \(N = \binom{n}{2}\) number pairwise dot products; \(\mathbf{} = (a_{12}, a_{13}, \dots, a_{n-1,n})\) multi-index exponents; \(|\mathbf{}| = \sum_{j<k} a_{jk}\) total degree term; \(\text{deg}_i(\mathbf{}) = \sum_{k \ne } a_{ik}\) "degree" vertex \(\) multigraph defined \(\mathbf{}\). Algorithmic Strategy: Unlike hardcoded implementations \(n=3\), function dynamically generates multi-indices \(\mathbf{}\) increasing total degrees \(d = 0, 1, 2, \dots\). uses recursive backtracking algorithm find weak compositions \(d\) \(N\) parts. Performance Limitations: Regarding convergence, series converges absolutely associated matrix \(M_n(C)\) positive definite, typically means cone vectors must close (cone must narrow); condition violated, series may produce meaningless results fail converge. terms computational complexity, number terms grows combinatorially \(n\) degree \(d\), \(n \ge 5\), calculating high-degree terms becomes computationally expensive. Convergence speed varies substantially: cones nearly orthogonal (dot products close 0), convergence fast, whereas cones high correlation generators (even positive definite), convergence can slow may require many terms achieve high precision; cases, Monte Carlo methods might efficient.

title: Spherical excess of a triangle via L'Huilier's theorem — lhuilier_angle
text: Given spherical triangle side lengths \(\), \(b\), \(c\) (measured great circle arcs radians), solid angle \(E\) : $$\tan\left(\frac{E}{4}\right) = \sqrt{\tan\left(\frac{s}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{s-}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{s-b}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{s-c}{2}\right)}$$ \(s = (+ b + c)/2\) semi-perimeter. Solving \(E\): $$E = 4 \arctan\left(\sqrt{\tan\left(\frac{s}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{s-}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{s-b}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{s-c}{2}\right)}\right)$$

what: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
text: Rotates vector \(\hat{x}\) aligned \(n\)-th canonical basis vector \(\hat{e}_n\) image aligned arbitrary unit direction \(\hat{\mu}\), \(O(n)\) operations using Givens rotation plane spanned \(\hat{e}_n\) \(\hat{\mu}\).

title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
code: rotate_from_canonical(x, mu_hat)

title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
text: x Numeric vector. Vector rotate (aligned n-th canonical axis). mu_hat Numeric vector. Target direction (unit vector).

title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
text: Numeric vector. Rotated vector \(\hat{y}\).

title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
text: function performs Givens rotation plane containing \(\hat{e}_n\) \(\hat{\mu}\). rotation : $$\hat{y} = \hat{x} + P(G - I_2)P^T\hat{x}$$ P orthonormal basis plane rotation, G 2D Givens rotation matrix, \(I_2\) 2×2 identity matrix. matrices defined : $$P = [\hat{e}_n, \frac{\hat{\mu} - \mu_n\hat{e}_n}   {\|\hat{\mu} - \mu_n\hat{e}_n\|}]$$ $$G = \begin{bmatrix} \mu_n & -\sqrt{1-\mu_n^2} \\   \sqrt{1-\mu_n^2} & \mu_n \end{bmatrix}$$ \(\mu_n = \hat{e}_n^T\hat{\mu}\). rotation costs O(n) operations, unlike general n-dimensional rotations cost O(n²).

title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical
text: Arun, ., & Venkatapathi, M. (2025). O(n) algorithm generating uniform random vectors n-dimensional cones. Sankhya , 87(2), 327-348. doi:10.1007/s13171-025-00387-9

title: Givens rotation from canonical axis to an arbitrary direction — rotate_from_canonical

text: two unit vectors \(v_1, v_2 \\mathbb{R}^2\) planar opening angle \([0, \pi]\) $$\theta = \mathrm{atan2}(|\det[v_1\ v_2]|,\ v_1 \cdot v_2),$$ normalized solid angle \(\Omega = \theta / (2\pi)\). atan2-based form numerically stable nearly orthogonal well nearly colinear inputs, dot-product/acos form loses precision near \(\pm 1\). title: Planar angle to solid-angle fraction in n dimensions — theta_to_omega
text: function \(\Theta: \mathbb{R} \\mathbb{R}\) maps planar cross-sectional angle \(\theta\) rotated solid angle fraction \(\Omega\) n dimensions: $$\Theta(\theta) = \begin{cases}   \frac{1}{2} (\sin^2\theta; \frac{n-1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}) &     \theta \[0, \frac{\pi}{2}] \\   1 - \frac{1}{2} (\sin^2\theta; \frac{n-1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}) &     \theta \(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi] \end{cases}$$ \((x; \alpha, \beta)\) regularized incomplete beta function.

what: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
text: Computes normalized solid angle simplicial cone whose Gram matrix \(V^\top V\) tridiagonal, using simplified series Fitisone & Zhou (2023, Theorem 4.1, equation 23). reduction \(\binom{n}{2}\) \(n - 1\) multi-index variables makes backend asymptotically faster general hypergeometric_series structure available.

title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
code: tridiagonal_series(V, max_terms = 1000, tol = 1e-10)

title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
text: V square \(n \times n\) numeric matrix whose columns cone generators. Need unit-normalized; columns rescaled internally. max_terms Integer. Hard cap number series terms accumulated truncation. Default 1000. tol Numeric. Per-degree convergence tolerance. Default 1e-10.

title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
text: list components solid_angle Normalized solid angle \([0, 1]\). n_terms Total number terms accumulated. converged Logical, TRUE per-degree contribution fell tol max_terms reached. beta Numeric vector length \(n - 1\) consecutive dot products \(\beta_i = v_i \cdot v_{+1}\). is_tridiagonal Logical flag, TRUE \(V^\top V\) passed tridiagonal test inside function.

title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
text: tridiagonal \(V^\top V\) Ribando series collapses $$\Omega(C) = \frac{|\det V|}{(4\pi)^{n/2}} \sum_{b \\mathbb{N}_0^{n-1}}         \frac{(-2)^{|b|}}{b!}\, \Gamma\!\left(\frac{1 + b_1}{2}\right)         \prod_{=2}^{n-1} \Gamma\!\left(\frac{1 + b_{-1} + b_i}{2}\right)         \Gamma\!\left(\frac{1 + b_{n-1}}{2}\right)\, \beta^{b},$$ \(\beta_i = v_i \cdot v_{+1}\). Theorem 4.1 Fitisone & Zhou (2023), tridiagonality \(V^\top V\) implies positive definiteness associated matrix \(M_n(C)\), series always converges absolutely. input satisfy tridiagonal test, function emits warning still iterates; result controlled approximation rather true solid angle trusted.

title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
text: Fitisone, ., & Zhou, Y. (2023). Solid angle measure polyhedral cones. arXiv:2304.11102 (math.CO). Theorem 4.1 equation (23). https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11102

title: Solid angle via the tridiagonal Fitisone-Zhou series — tridiagonal_series
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # 4D cone with only consecutive dot products non-zero v1 <- c(1, 0, 0, 0) v2 <- c(0.8, 0.6, 0, 0) v3 <- c(0, 0.6, 0.8, 0) v4 <- c(0, 0, 0.7, 0.7) / sqrt(0.98) V  <- cbind(v1, v2, v3, v4) res <- tridiagonal_series(V, max_terms = 500) res$solid_angle res$is_tridiagonal     # TRUE } # }

title: SolidAngleR 0.6.0
text: omega() removed. multivariate-normal orthant integration now exposed "mvn" branch dispatcher; call compute_solid_angle(V, method = "mvn") instead. new branch returns scalar normalized solid angle directly; per-dimension geometric mean previously available omega(V)$omega_scaled recovered compute_solid_angle(V, method = "mvn")^(1 / ncol(V)).

title: SolidAngleR 0.6.0
text: compute_solid_angle() gains method = "mvn", dispatching mvtnorm::pmvnorm() positive orthant via Genz-Bretz quasi-Monte Carlo algorithm. Emits condition-number high-dimension warnings deleted omega().

title: SolidAngleR 0.6.0
text: Complete roxygen rewrite across every exported symbol: explicit @title sentence case, expanded @description @details LaTeX equations, verified @references DOI/ISBN, runnable @examples, bidirectional @seealso links S3 constructor diagnose_cone() print, summary, plot methods. Internal helpers consistently marked @noRd; section headers across R/ normalised canonical triple-line convention. _pkgdown.yml reference index reorganised ten functional groups (main interface, low-dimensional formulas, series methods, geometric decomposition methods, Monte Carlo sampling, cone diagnostics, cone structure utilities, geometry primitives, visualisation, S3 methods). Vignettes: heading-spacing convention enforced across seven articles; chunk evaluation vignette .theoretical-analysis.Rmd set uniformly eval = FALSE. 2D plots vignettes b, c, d, f, g, histogram, density, validation, performance, vMF rejection-comparison panels e, converted ggplot2 subtitle grey caption per package plot-default rule. Two diagrammatic visualisations e (Givens rotation arrow plot Lambertian ray-tracing side view) intentionally retained base graphics, arrow / normal annotations clearer ggplot equivalent.

title: SolidAngleR 0.5.1
text: tridiagonal_series(): default convergence tolerance relaxed .Machine$double.eps (2.2e-16) 1e-10, eliminating spurious non-convergence well-posed tridiagonal cones whose signed residuals sit double-precision noise level. Callers need previous strict behaviour must pass tol = .Machine$double.eps explicitly. Numerical-stability corrections closed-form, series geometric backends (formulas_2d.R, formulas_3d.R, geometric_methods.R, series_hypergeometric.R, series_tridiagonal.R) compiled sampling layer (cone_sampling.cpp, cone_sampling.R), removing silent NaN outputs near-degenerate configurations.

title: SolidAngleR 0.5.0
text: Class cone_diagnosis gains full S3 triad: new methods summary.cone_diagnosis(), print.summary.cone_diagnosis() plot.cone_diagnosis(). diagnose_cone() returns first-class diagnostic object full print, summary plot lifecycle. compute_solid_angle() dispatch path extended: method = "auto" internal router now consults cone_diagnosis object instead recomputing spectral tridiagonal tests every call.

title: SolidAngleR 0.1.0
text: First public release. Forty-three exported functions covering full stack solid-angle methods polyhedral cones arbitrary dimension. closed forms n = 2 n = 3 exposed solid_angle_2d(), solid_angle_2d_inner(), solid_angle_3d(), solid_angle_3d_det(), solid_angle_3d_from_rays(), solid_angle_polyhedral() spherical_triangle_area(). Aomoto-Ribando hypergeometric series positive-definite cones n = 2, 3 available hypergeometric_series(), Fitisone-Zhou tridiagonal specialisation tridiagonal_series(). recursive Brion-Vergne decomposition, lifts positive-definiteness restriction, exposed decompose_cone() solid_angle_decomposition(). Mazonka’s geometric formulas right circular, segmental, surface intersecting cones wrapped solid_angle_cone(), solid_angle_cone_segment(), solid_angle_conical_surface(), solid_angle_intersecting_cones() plotIntersectingCones(). Feasibility-domain computations via multivariate-normal integration delivered omega(), Monte Carlo estimator solid_angle_monte_carlo(). pure-R uniform--cone sampler stack includes generate_cone_sample(), generate_cone_samples(), generate_hollow_cone_sample(), generate_point_on_sphere(), theta_to_omega(), omega_to_theta(), generate_planar_angle_inverse(), generate_planar_angle_rejection(), rotate_from_canonical(), rejection_cost() verify_cone_uniformity(). Matrix cone utilities provided compute_associated_matrix(), compute_dot_product_matrix(), is_positive_definite(), is_tridiagonal(), is_linearly_independent(), normalize_vectors(), create_tridiagonal_cone(), cross_product_3d(), angle_between() lhuilier_angle(). Extreme-ray extraction handled generate_spanning_trees(). main dispatcher compute_solid_angle(), batch form compute_solid_angles(), diagnostic constructor diagnose_cone() print.cone_diagnosis() method.

title: SolidAngleR 0.1.0
text: Three correctness fixes predate first public commit recorded provenance. First, operator-precedence bug gamma(1 + x / 2) replaced correct gamma((1 + x) / 2) throughout hypergeometric_series_2d(), hypergeometric_series_3d() tridiagonal_series(); incorrect form produced approximately tenfold errors solid-angle computations. Second, every geometric backend renormalised return values [0, 1]: solid_angle_cone(), solid_angle_polyhedral(), solid_angle_cone_segment() solid_angle_intersecting_cones() previously returned steradians now consistent series Monte Carlo backends. Third, spurious names attributes stripped compute_solid_angle() solid_angle_decomposition() return values.
